short_description: Filovirus whose defining feature is its SHAPE: a uniformly ~80 nm wide, up to 1000+ nm long thread with an extreme aspect ratio, its end typically curled into a shepherd's-crook hook (U-, 6- and open-loop forms are equally authentic). A host-derived lipid envelope studded with short club-shaped glycoprotein (GP) spikes ~10 nm apart wraps a matrix layer and a ~50 nm helical nucleocapsid whose regular cross-striations run ACROSS the filament; inside it lies one 19 kb negative-sense RNA strand with just seven genes. It enters macrophages, monocytes and dendritic cells first and endothelium later, lives between outbreaks in fruit bats, spreads only by direct contact with body fluids and never through the air, and has had a licensed vaccine since 2019.

morphology.shape: filamentous, extreme aspect ratio (a thread, NOT a sphere and NOT a short bacillus-like rod); pleomorphic in the sense that the SAME uniform-width filament also occurs branched, U-shaped, 6-shaped, circular or open-looped. Spherical forms are rare to absent.
morphology.diameter_nm: ~80 nm for the envelope itself; ICTV gives 96-98 nm for the whole particle including the surface spikes. The width is remarkably CONSTANT along the entire length.
morphology.length_nm: highly variable, commonly ~800-1000 nm and occasionally far longer (filaments to >20 um are reported); the particle length of PEAK INFECTIVITY is ~805 nm for ebolaviruses. ViralZone quotes 970 nm as the typical figure.
morphology.signature_silhouette: the end curled into a shepherd's crook / question-mark hook. In the CDC's own cryo-EM particle counts for the sister genus, roughly a third of particles were filamentous, a third 6-shaped and a third round-looped, so the hook is the signature but the loop forms are equally real.
morphology.envelope: host-derived lipid bilayer taken from the plasma membrane of the cell the virion budded from.
morphology.spikes: trimeric GP1,2 glycoprotein spikes, SHORT and club-shaped, ~7-10 nm long, spaced at ~10 nm intervals, EVENLY distributed over the whole filament surface (not a sparse corona, not long stalked clubs).
morphology.matrix: VP40 forms the matrix layer lining the inner leaflet of the envelope and drives budding of the filament; VP24 is a second, minor membrane-associated protein.
morphology.nucleocapsid: helical ribonucleoprotein tube running the whole length of the filament. Outer diameter 45-50 nm with an electron-dense central axis of 19-25 nm; the helical capsid shows CROSS-STRIATIONS at a ~5 nm interval in negative stain. In-vitro cryo-EM of the Ebola NP assembly gives outer/inner diameters of 49 nm / 33 nm and a helical pitch of 11.2 nm (~42 asymmetric units per turn); in-virion cryo-ET of Marburg gives a left-handed helix of 7.5 nm pitch with ~15 protrusions per turn. Report the striation as a transverse repeat, not a single canonical number.
morphology.genome: ONE linear, non-segmented, negative-sense single-stranded RNA of 18,959-18,961 nt (~19 kb), fully sheathed in NP and associated with VP35, VP30 and the L polymerase. Exactly SEVEN genes, gene order 3'-NP-VP35-VP40-GP-VP30-VP24-L-5'.
morphology.tropism: macrophages, monocytes and dendritic cells are the first cells entered; endothelial cells, hepatocytes and adrenal cortical cells follow later in infection. Entry is by macropinocytosis, cathepsin cleavage of GP in the endosome and binding to the endosomal receptor NPC1.
morphology.ecology: fruit bats of the Pteropodidae are the presumed reservoir; spillover to humans is rare. Human-to-human spread requires DIRECT CONTACT with blood or body fluids or contaminated surfaces - it is not airborne.

colour_legend.envelope: warm dusty coral-salmon translucent lipid bilayer (the filament's outer skin)
colour_legend.gp_spike: muted slate periwinkle-blue, short club-headed knobs on very short stalks, evenly spaced over the whole surface
colour_legend.matrix_vp40: pale sage-green thin layer lining the envelope from inside
colour_legend.nucleocapsid: coppery amber tube with fine regular TRANSVERSE bands (the cross-striation)
colour_legend.rna: deep indigo-plum single continuous thread inside the amber tube
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (watercolour: warm aged cream paper, full bleed)
colour_legend.note: A virion has no colour of its own and electron microscopes image in greyscale, so every colour here is teaching convention (reference/colors.md). The chosen CDC reference is a digitally COLORIZED TEM (blue filaments on a red-stained field) - its palette is likewise an artist's choice, not the virus. Keep this structure->colour mapping identical across textbook, sem, 3d and watercolor so the set reads as one poster.

do_not_draw: a SPHERE, ball, blob or round particle of any kind - the defining property of this virus is that it is a long thin THREAD; a spherical Ebola virion is the single most serious error possible here
a short stubby rod, bacillus, capsule or sausage shape with an aspect ratio anywhere near 3:1 - the filament is at least ten times longer than it is wide and runs out of the frame
a filament whose width swells and narrows along its length - the ~80 nm diameter is essentially CONSTANT from end to end
a rigid icosahedral capsid, a geometric shell, a polyhedral core or a d20-die silhouette - the interior is a flexible helical tube
DNA, a double helix, base-pair rungs or a ladder genome - the genome is a single negative-sense RNA strand
a segmented genome, eight little rods or eleven separate pieces - there is exactly ONE continuous RNA molecule

LENGTHWISE stripes, longitudinal grooves or cables running ALONG the filament's long axis in place of the cross-striation - the nucleocapsid's regular bands run ACROSS the width, like a stack of coins seen edge-on
long stalked coronavirus-style club spikes standing far apart in a sparse corona - the GP spikes are short, blunt and densely, evenly spaced
a dense mat, tangle, nest, bundle or ball of many filaments filling the frame - one single readable virion is the teaching subject
a bacteriophage head-and-tail body, tail fibres, base plate, legs, flagellum, pilus, cell wall or capsule
a nucleus, ribosomes, mitochondria or any cell organelle - a virion is not a cell

blood, blood cells, bleeding, wounds, rashes, skulls, biohazard symbols, warning triangles, hazmat suits, monsters, teeth, claws, faces or any menacing or anthropomorphic treatment - this is a lethal disease and the atlas shows it soberly
any baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, rulers, legends or watermarks
a black border, dark frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet or card lying on a surface

reference.modality: transmission electron microscopy (TEM), thin section / negative contrast, DIGITALLY COLORIZED (blue virions on a red-tinted field) - the colour is an artist's addition, the microscope images in greyscale
reference.verified: Downloaded and viewed at 1200 px wide: four long, uniformly thin filaments of constant width lie across a granular stained field; the leftmost one curls into a closed loop and a hook at its left end. No text, no scale bar, no border anywhere in the plate.
reference.note: This is the canonical teaching plate for Ebola morphology and shows exactly what the brief asks for: constant-width threads with a curled/hooked end. It is WIDE (2.17:1), so a centred square crop would cut the hook away - a deterministic left-hand square crop is used instead, keeping the hook and letting the filaments run off the right edge.

fallbacks.note: The 1976 original plate; greyscale, lower contrast, would need false-colouring.
